1.0.2:
- AI Takeoff: AI items stay out of the totals until you accept them - in the Review Queue, or select a dashed AI markup and press A (accept) or D (deny).
- Fix takeoff on the drawing: drag an outline's corners, drag a box (or Ctrl+click) to select several and move or delete them together. The Markups List has an Origin column.
- Missed counts: right-click a count > Show Uncounted Copies; Report Missed in the Review Queue then box one copy to find the rest.
- Count Library: keep the symbols you count on every job and try them on the next plan set.
- Count by Label lists every hit first, with wildcards (P-# finds P-1 to P-12).
- AI Takeoff zones (Only Here / Leave Out) and item names it learns from you.
- Rooms no longer count shared floor twice; fire extinguishers are found on the life safety plans.
Help > Help Center & Tutorials has a lesson for each.
1.0.3:
- AI Takeoff rooms: the floor beside a shower bench, a door swing or a grab bar is now counted, so rooms such as showers no longer measure short there. The floor under a built-in bench itself still isn't counted - those rooms are flagged for review.
- Also in this version (from 1.0.2): accept or deny AI markups with A / D, reshape outlines by their corners, the Count Library, Count by Label wildcards (P-#), AI Takeoff zones and learned item names.
Help > Help Center & Tutorials has a lesson for each.
1.0.4:
- Tool sets for the team: save them as a file and others double-click it to get the same tools; tools can carry a unit cost, columns, rise/drop or wall height. A metric set is included (Tool Sets > Restore Default Tools).
- Live legends for a page or the whole set, limited to chosen tool sets.
- Wall Area (Shift+W): length x height less openings. Right-click a measurement for Rise / Drop, Convert To, Show Volume In and Copy Several Times; right-click a count to add more to it.
- Scale presets ask which pages and warn about half-size prints. Takeoff > Show Side Lengths and Captions.
- Markups List: group by any column, export to Excel or XML. Proposals can list what the takeoff assumed. Takeoff > Takeoff Standard checklist.
Help > Help Center & Tutorials has a lesson for each.
1.0.5:
- Drawing sets with a lot of markups open quickly - a set with over 30,000 markups that froze on open now opens in a couple of seconds. For sets that big the Markups List starts with the current page; untick This page to list them all.
- File > Print Preview shows each page on its paper before it prints. Printing shows which page is going out (Printing page 13 of 60), with Cancel.
- Also in this version (from 1.0.4): tool sets for the team, live legends, Wall Area (Shift+W), rise/drop, Convert To, Copy Several Times and the Takeoff Standard checklist.
Help > Help Center & Tutorials has a lesson for each.
1.0.6:
- Copy text from a drawing: Home > Select Text (I), drag across the words, Ctrl+C. Box a schedule and press Ctrl+Shift+C to paste it into Excel with its columns. Double-click a word, or select a text box and Ctrl+C.
- Help > Report an Issue: say what happened, check the screenshot, and an email to support opens with it attached. After the program stops responding, the next start offers to report it.
- Tools > Package Tracker: FedEx, UPS, USPS and DHL numbers in one list (paste a shipping email and they're picked out), expected dates, late packages in red, one click opens the carrier's tracking page.
- AI Takeoff rooms now count the floor under a built-in shower bench.
- Hold the mouse wheel button and drag to pan.
- On a shared (server) install, Check for Updates offers your own copy that updates itself - no IT visit needed.
- Bid gate in Error Check: old prices, expired quotes, unpriced addenda (they block the bid form), placeholders and double counts. Estimate > Placeholders & Allowances and Escalation to Buy Date.
- Estimate > Leveling Board: sub quotes against your scope in green / yellow / red, gaps plugged from your own takeoff, the low into the estimate. Scope sheets per trade from the takeoff and specs.
- Estimate > Bid Form Autopilot fills the owner's bid form; Billing > Change Order From Revision prices a revised sheet with clouded backup; bid results and hit rate by size and markup in the Dashboard.
- File > Open Bid Download (.zip) as a Job; Review > Spec Book Risk Scanner; Tools > Time Log; right-click actions in File Explorer.
Help > Help Center & Tutorials has a lesson for each.
1.0.7:
- Estimate > Bid Form Workbook: pick the spec book or the owner's bid form and QuantiSheet makes an Excel workbook of its items, quantities and alternates. Type the unit prices in the yellow cells; line totals, the subtotal, add and deduct alternates and the base bid are Excel formulas. Transfer to PDF fills the bid form and adds a bid schedule page whose fields add and subtract on their own.
- Check an Addendum (in the Bid Form Workbook): if an addendum reissues the bid form, you see what changed (new items, removed items, quantity changes, alternates) and get a new workbook with the prices kept for items that didn't change. Every addendum summary now says when the addendum includes a bid form.
- Spec Book Risk Scanner: each scan saves '<project> - Bid Form & Insurance Review.pdf' beside the spec book with the bid form, insurance requirements and builder's risk pages pulled out behind a cover page.
- Estimate > Builder's Risk Quote Request: project name, address, summary of work and estimated amount on one page, with the spec's builder's risk pages attached. Edit anything, then Email to Insurance sends it from QuantiSheet; the agent's address is remembered.
- Count From a Picture: paste or pick a picture of a symbol and every match on the sheet (or all sheets) is found for review.
- Bid quotes that are scans or photos are read with text recognition; the Bid Form Autopilot fills unit prices from the estimate; the dashboard shows estimating hours from the Time Log.
- Package Tracker: with a carrier's developer keys (Carrier Keys…), Check Status shows each package's latest scan and delivery date in the list.
1.1.1:
- Fixed: clicking QuantiSheet sometimes opened it twice. It now opens one window (File > New Window when you want a second).
- Fewer clicks: pick your role (Estimator, PM, Service, Office) and the tabs and quick bar fit it. Fewer tabs; a one-time card after this update lets you pick a role or put the old tabs back (also View > Ribbon Tabs). Buy Quantities, Typical Sheet, Carry Forward and Tags Check are on the Takeoff tab, Bid Form Workbook and Builder's Risk on the Estimate tab; one Compare button opens overlay, changes and text.
- Quick bar: right-click any button > Pin to Quick Bar; drag pins to reorder. One Export button remembers your last export.
- Right-click the drawing: Set Scale, Length, Area, Count, Edit Text Here, Redact Area, Snapshot, New RFI Here, Paste Here, Rotate This Page, Insert Pages Here.
- Ctrl+K finds sheets, takeoff items, RFIs and service records too; Shift+Enter shows where a button lives. F10 or Alt opens the menus from the keyboard. Help > Customize Shortcuts.
- Takeoff: number keys 1-9 pick Tool Chest tools and Space repeats the last tool. Copy and paste takeoff between sheets (re-measured at the new sheet's scale). Buy Quantities turns totals into sheets, boxes or rolls with waste. Tags vs Schedule Check, Carry Takeoff Forward, Typical Sheet, Color Takeoff By, Show Only This Item, Bulk Edit, Join and Split runs, arcs (Tab). Overlapping cutouts are counted once.
- A scale read from the title block stays marked "unconfirmed" (also after saving and on other PCs) and asks to be checked before your first measurement on that sheet. Opening a set no longer asks to save just because scales were read.
- New Service tab: calls, agreements, logs and tests (including a backflow test report), pricing, records and quotes.
- Back Office (Project > Office): Waiting on Me, crew board with Copy Yesterday's Crews, checklist templates, safety meetings, pre-task plans (sign and PDF), incidents (people, photos, recordable log), equipment (units and hours), warranty calls (assignee, photos, report), job cost report import with a preview and a duplicate check, duplicate invoices held for a reason, a separate approver, and Payroll Key & Approvals (it asks for a key backup until you make one).
- Safer files: a warning before a save breaks a signature; redacted text is really removed; takeoff data that drops off an emailed PDF can be put back; a file from a newer version won't be overwritten; "someone else has this open" on shared folders.
- Tools > Back Up My QuantiSheet Data and Restore (plus a weekly automatic backup). Sage export shows a preview and saves an undo file. Macros are checked before they run.
- Help > Check for Updates Now; Help > About shows "Up to date" and when it last checked. Updates are checked before they install, and the installer of the version you're on is kept so you can reinstall it.
- Also new since 1.0.6: Bid Form Workbook and Check an Addendum, Spec Book Risk Scanner, Builder's Risk Quote Request, Count From a Picture, and Package Tracker status.
- Simple Menus is gone: View > Layout offers Modern or Full Ribbon + Tool Rail. If you were on Simple Menus, you'll start on the ribbon.
- A file that won't open now says why and what to do; a damaged PDF can be repaired into a copy (your file isn't changed).
- Undo says what it takes back ("Undo Bulk Edit (412 items)"). A redaction can be undone until you save.
- Help > Practice Job walks through a whole first job in about 10 minutes.
1.1.2:
- New look: green ribbon tiles, a PDF Management tab with every PDF tool in one place (Edit PDF first), an AI tab, and the Takeoff tab always on the ribbon. The window's title bar follows the dark theme.
- Service: invoices now carry sales tax (pick the rate; "Make default"), a member discount and a credit card fee, each on its own line and in the export to Back Office, Sage and hh2. New Service Settings window (Service > Service Settings) for the card fee %, default tax, invoice terms, member discount and agreement visits. Agreements keep the discount they were sold with.
- Service, also new: good / better / best quotes, changeout proposals, tune-up planner, maintenance checklists, a leave-behind report, warranty registrations, permits, callbacks and history, phone tickets, technician hours to Back Office time cards, refrigerant recovery and cylinder records with a repair clock and year-end list, and the backflow test report on your water district's own form (bring the district's form and use Map the Form once to set it up). The refrigerant rules built in have not yet been reviewed against the regulations: check its thresholds and dates before you rely on them.
- Money rounds the normal way everywhere (a 5 rounds up): bids, proposals, assemblies, labor rates, pay applications, retainage, Project Manager and the bid pages. Each line is rounded the same way as its total, so lines add up to the total to the cent. A proposal shows the same price in every format. Number fields refuse what they can't read ("1.000,50", more than a trillion) instead of guessing, and Service refuses an amount over $100 million.
- Estimates: a unit cost typed on a takeoff line now carries into the proposal, the bid build-up, the exports and Build From Estimate, under its cost type (material when none is picked). Before, it counted in the Estimate total only. A measured quantity is priced as shown, to 2 decimals, so quantity x unit cost checks by hand; a quantity you type is priced exactly as typed. Both can move the total on an existing job by a few cents, or by the typed prices that were left out: re-check open bids. If a group is priced by an assembly and also has a unit cost typed on its line, both count: use one.
- Display: Rotate View fits the turned page; column headers and window titles that were cut off are shown in full; a unit cost shows as typed (4.125, not 4.13); Work Order fields are labelled.
- Pay applications: each line's retainage adds up to the retainage on the summary page. A little work never prints as "0%".
- Assemblies: formulas from an imported price list are checked once and repaired where an old version read them wrong.
- AI Summary, Redline and Spec Check read the whole document by default and say what they read. Redline and Spec Check show how long each part has waited, skip a part that doesn't answer in 5 minutes, can be stopped (Stop, then Stop Now), and say exactly which pages were not reviewed. Summary has a Stop button and the same 5-minute limit. The summary lists the sheets in the set apart from sheets only referenced, takes out abbreviation meanings the drawings don't define, and marks a sheet number or drawing scale that isn't in the drawings. It is still a draft to check against the drawings.
- Translate Markups runs in the background, keeps its result, says how many comments came back translated, and Cancel really ends the request.
- AI server set by your IT department: the Local AI Models window follows it too.
- Protected PDFs stay protected: Reduce File Size, Watermark and batch actions keep the password and permissions, and never change the file you have open. Reduce File Size uses less memory on big files and keeps the original when the result isn't smaller.
- Copy Back to the job folder no longer fails with "file in use" after the drawing was open in a tab.
- ADA checker: faster on big sets, its counts can be undone and are shared in a live session, and a parking stall marked both Parking and Accessible counts once.
- Accessibility Check: each automatic fix is its own Undo step; fixing no longer resets the viewer settings saved in the file.
- Aerial and site layers: a clear message when a map service sends too much or something unreadable; a rotated or stretched image file is refused instead of placed at the wrong scale.
- Project Manager: a save that happened while you were still typing could fail; fixed.
- Export to Excel keeps leading zeros in codes. Card-number search for redaction no longer flags ordinary long numbers.
- Back Office: the billing register refreshes after a change.
- Help: four pages pointed at the wrong tab; fixed.
1.1.3:
- Auto Takeoff rooms: much more accurate. Each room's outline is now put back on the drawing's own wall lines, so small rooms and closets no longer measure an inch short all round. On our hard test plans every tagged room is found and 99% are within 2% of the true area (before: two rooms in three found, one in five within 2%). Rooms behind shut, double, pocket and bifold doors, closets, shafts and rooms with angled walls are found. A table or a toilet is no longer read as a door swing. Areas are still a draft to check: a room the program is unsure of is flagged.
- Auto Takeoff walls: walls are paired pen by pen, so a wall face is no longer paired with a counter edge or a fixture. Wall length on our test plans went from 7.6% over to within 2%, in the right thicknesses.
- Faster on big jobs: a markup on a sheet with 500 markups (about twice as fast), entering progress on a pay application late in a job (about six times as fast), switching theme and Field Mode. Files with large estimates and billing save smaller.
- Sturdier: damaged or odd markup data in a file is skipped instead of stopping the page; an amount too large to be money is refused with a message; a number field holding something that is not a number counts as zero in the bid build-up.
1.1.4:
- Exclusions side by side: who excludes what. A new Exclusions tab in the Leveling window, and a button on the Leveling Board and on Scope Sheets (Compare Exclusions). One row per exclusion, one column per bidder; each cell says excluded, included or not stated, in the bidder's own words. An exclusion only one bidder has is marked ONLY ONE. Similar wordings share a row: right-click to split one off or merge two rows. It exports with the leveling report. One click prices an exclusion: on a Scope Sheet it puts the $ on that bidder's exclusion row (still Pending until you accept it); in the Leveling window it adds an adjustment.
- Qualification at a glance: each bidder shows insurance, license, bonding against this bid (single-job limit) and prequalification, from the Company Directory, on the Leveling window, Leveling Board, Scope Sheets and the Bid-Day sheet. Awarding to a bidder with expired insurance or license, or a bid over the bonding or approved limit, asks for a reason first; the reason is kept with the award. The Company Directory has a new License expires date.
- Show where a number came from: every value read from a sub's proposal keeps its page and place. Right-click a price in the Leveling matrix or on the Leveling Board, press Show Source on a Scope Sheet row, or double-click a cell in the Exclusions table, and the quote opens with the words boxed. Works on scanned quotes when OCR is installed.
- Read with AI, for a proposal the program couldn't read in full (lines not read, or lines that don't add up): Read a Proposal with AI in the Leveling window, Read a Quote with AI on the Leveling Board, Import with AI on a Scope Sheet. The AI on this PC reads it; nothing leaves the computer, and it runs only when you ask, with a Stop button and a 5-minute limit. Only values that are in the quote word for word are offered; anything else the model says is thrown out and counted. Each offer is marked AI, check and is added only when you tick it. Lines that don't add up to the total are flagged, never changed to fit. It is still a draft to check against the quote.
1.1.5:
- Variance against our own estimate, line by line: a Variance button on the Leveling Board and on Scope Sheets. For each scope row it shows our number, each bidder's number and the difference in $ and %, and marks rows HIGH or LOW at a percent you set (15% to start; it is kept as your setting). Scope we carry that a bidder didn't price or excluded is listed per bidder at our dollar value, the same dollars the leveling plugs. A blank is not $0.00, and a row we have no number for says no estimate instead of 0%. The rows add up to the leveled total to the cent. Export to Excel or PDF.
- Bid forms: a new line type, Scope item, that each bidder marks Included or Excluded on the bid page (template: Scope checklist). Bidders now list inclusions, exclusions and clarifications one per line. On a Scope Sheet, the from-package button also brings in each bidder's answers: included / excluded flags, prices, and their exclusions and clarifications as Pending rows - nothing retyped, and cells you already filled in are left alone. Lines you ask on every package (bid bond, addenda, schedule) can be kept once per project: Bid Form > Project-wide lines. Print Bid Form saves the form as a PDF in the project's Bid Forms folder; nothing is sent. If you host your own hub server, update it so bidders see the Included / Excluded choice; the program tells you when an invitation went through an older hub.
- Bid Board (Estimate > Bid Board): every invitation to bid that comes to you in one list - project, GC, trade, bid date and time, job walk, questions due, estimator, your notes, and status (Undecided, Accepted, Submitted, Won, Lost, Declined). Add one by typing it in, or From Email to read a saved invitation (.eml, or pasted text) into a draft you check and save; nothing is sent and the email is not changed. An invitation that looks like a project already on the board (a similar name with a close bid date, or the same address, even from another GC) is flagged with the reason, and rows for the same project are marked so it is priced once. Go / No-Go gives a score and a recommendation from a short checklist with weights you can change; you decide, and your reason is kept. The Calendar tab lists the dates and exports a calendar file (.ics). Results shows win rate by GC (Won and Lost only), bids per month and each estimator's open bids; the Estimating Dashboard's hit rate can be grouped by GC (bid to). An Outlook .msg file isn't read: save the email as .eml or paste its text.
- Fill From the Job and Sign (Fill & Sign menu), for forms that come back to be filled and signed: each fillable field is listed with the value it would get and where that value comes from (your company settings, the job's billing info, the Company Directory for a sub's form, today's date). Fields the program is sure of start ticked; ones it is unsure of are marked to check and start unticked; a field it can't place is left for you. Tax IDs, Social Security numbers and bank details are never kept or filled. Fill Ticked writes a new file and leaves your form as it was. Sign Selected Box puts your saved signature in that one box, in a new file, and records who signed, when and the file's fingerprint in the file's audit trail and in Signed Forms Log.csv beside it. It is a drawn signature, not a certificate signature. Nothing is sent.
- Your drawn signature and initials are no longer kept in the settings file as plain text: they are stored encrypted for your Windows account, and moved there the first time they are used.
